unit.description: FastAPI process exposing the kloc-agent REST + SSE + internal-ingestion surfaces, hosting the in-process EventBus, the ExecutionRegistry replay ring, and the RunnerRegistry that spawns one runner container per Session. Single uvicorn worker (process- local dicts gate run-id routing). Listens on container port 8000, published on host port 8002 in dev compose.

Next.js 16 / React 19 single-page chat surface for the Analyst. Renders the Session list, the conversation view, the pending Assistant indicator, Tool Call indicators (running / completed / denied), and Artifact chips. Ships as a Next.js standalone server (node server.js on port 3000) that also hosts the BFF route handlers that proxy the SSE stream.

Next.js route handlers under `/api/agent-proxy*`, co-resident with `top.frontend` in the same Node process but a logically distinct unit. POSTs new runs and GETs reconnects are proxied through here so the browser only ever talks to its same-origin Next server; the BFF then opens a chunked `text/event-stream` connection to `top.backend` and pipes the upstream body straight back to the browser unchanged.

Per-Session container running `python -m runner` under `opentelemetry-instrument`. Reads its HydrationPayload from `/run/kloc/.json` (RO bind-mount), opens MCP clients, builds a Strands `Agent` wrapped by `ag_ui_strands.StrandsAgent`, long-polls the backend inbox for user-message frames, runs each turn, and streams AG-UI events back over a chunked NDJSON POST. Memory cap 1 GiB, 2 nano-CPUs, pids-limit 256, no restart policy.
unit.tech: Python 3.12, Strands Agent SDK, ag_ui_strands wrapper, httpx, MCP Python SDK

unit.description: Authoritative durable store for the kloc-agent domain state: `sessions`, `messages` (per-Session monotonic `seq`), `audit_log` (locked vocabulary of 12 event names), `artifact_metadata` (idempotent on `(session_id, object_key)`). Also hosts the PGMQ extension which holds one durable inbox queue per Session (`inbox_{session_id_no_dashes}`) — the backend-to-runner transport for user-message frames, paired with `NOTIFY inbox_{slug}` for sub-millisecond wake-up of the runner's `LISTEN`. Queue rows survive runner eviction and backend restart in the same WAL that protects `messages` and `audit_log`. Reached over async asyncpg (pool size 10, max overflow 20, pre-ping). Image swapped from `postgres:16-alpine` to a pgmq-bundled flavour (`quay.io/tembo/pg16-pgmq:latest`).

S3-compatible blob store holding Artifact bodies the runner uploads during a turn. Backend never writes content here — it issues presigned GET URLs (900 s expiry) so the browser can download an Artifact via a `Location:` redirect from the backend. Bucket `kloc-agent-artifacts-dev` created by the `mc-init` compose helper at boot.

Docker-managed named volume `kloc-hydration` mounted `/tmp/kloc-hydration` (backend, RW) and `/run/kloc` (each runner, RO). Backend writes one `.json` per spawn; the runner reads it once at startup. Named-volume rather than bind-mount because the backend container's relative paths don't resolve on the host the way aiodocker sees them.

Docker-managed named volume `kloc-skills` seeded from `./skills/` by the `skills-init` compose helper. Mounted `/skills-source` (backend, RO) and `/skills` (each runner, RO). Holds the SKILL.md files the runner discovers via `agentskills.discover_skills` to assemble its system prompt.

The host's Docker engine. Reached by the backend over the bind-mounted unix socket `/var/run/docker.sock`. The backend uses aiodocker (Docker-outside-of-Docker, sibling-container pattern) to create / start / inspect / stop / delete per-Session runner containers on the shared `kloc` bridge network. The unix socket bind-mount is mandatory; lifespan fails loudly without it.

External Streamable-HTTP MCP server fronting the operator's kloc-intelligence code-search stack (Neo4j + Qdrant + `mcp-server-http`). Reached from each runner container at `http://host.docker.internal:8765/mcp` (default). Brought up by the operator out of band; the runner treats it as an opaque MCP endpoint and binds whatever `list_tools_sync()` returns into the Strands agent.

The selected LLM provider: Anthropic Messages API or Google Gemini API (default `gemini` per dev compose). Called from inside each runner container by the Strands model adapter the `model_factory` selects from `llm_provider` in the HydrationPayload. `openrouter` and `bedrock` are stubbed paths, not wired.

The Analyst's web browser. Renders `top.frontend` pages, opens an `EventSource`-style streaming `fetch` against `top.frontend-bff` for each Assistant turn, and follows the 302 redirect to MinIO when an Artifact chip is clicked. Out of the system boundary.

communication.note: Browser fetches the Next.js HTML/CSS/JS bundle and renders the SPA. No documented contract — this is the SPA shell, not an API surface.

The browser fetches the public REST surface directly from `top.backend` (host port 8002 in dev compose, behind permissive CORS). The artifact GET returns 302 to a presigned MinIO URL the browser follows itself.
Server-side fetch from `app/s/[sessionId]/page.tsx` — `Promise.all([getSession, listMessages])` — to hydrate the conversation surface on first render.

Browser opens a `fetch` against `/api/agent-proxy` (POST, submit) or `/api/agent-proxy/resume` (GET, reconnect) and reads the SSE body progressively. Direction is server→client streaming after the initial request, hence `stream-push`. Cursor replay on reconnect via `last_event_id`.
BFF opens the same shape upstream and pipes the response body back to the browser unchanged. Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform; Connection: keep-alive.

Async asyncpg connection pool. Reads + writes for sessions, messages, audit_log, artifact_metadata. Pure OLTP — the inbox transport now flows over a separate logical edge (`top.com.backend-to-postgres-inbox`) even though it shares the same asyncpg pool.

One round-trip per user-message: `pgmq.send(queue, payload)` paired with `NOTIFY inbox_{slug}` in the same transaction so the runner's `LISTEN` wakes the moment the row commits. Queue name is derived from `session_id` alone (`inbox_{session_id_no_dashes}`), NOT from any per-spawn registry entry — that is what structurally eliminates the "identity drift on eviction" failure class.

aioboto3 S3 client. Used to issue presigned GET URLs and for the `readyz` `list_buckets` liveness probe. Backend does not write artifact bodies — the runner uploads directly, the backend only stores metadata.

The runner uploads Artifact bytes directly to MinIO during a turn, then sends `ArtifactRegistered` to the backend so `artifact_metadata` is inserted. Bucket and key are derived from `artifact_object_key(session_id, artifact_id, filename)`.
aiodocker over the bind-mounted `/var/run/docker.sock`. create / start / stop(t=5) / wait / delete and label-filtered `list` for the boot-time orphan sweep.
Backend writes `.json` to `/tmp/kloc-hydration/` before each spawn so the runner can read it at `/run/kloc/.json` on first boot. Written once per spawn, never updated.
Read-only mount. The runner reads its hydration file once at startup; the 4 MiB cap is enforced before parsing.
Backend mounts `kloc-skills` read-only at `/skills-source` (the active seeding is owned by the `skills-init` helper, not the backend at runtime).
Runner reads SKILL.md files from `/skills` (RO) to build its system prompt at startup.

Single long-lived chunked POST whose body is a JSONL stream of AG-UI events and runner liveness heartbeats. Reconnect-on- failure with backoff (0.5..10 s) replays the in-flight attempt transcript on the next attempt — over-delivery preferred to silent loss of terminal frames.

Single long-lived asyncpg connection per runner. Issues `LISTEN inbox_{slug}` on attach, then alternates `pgmq.read(queue, vt=300, qty=1)` (consume) and `pgmq.delete( queue, msg_id)` (ack-after-process). The `NOTIFY` from the backend's enqueue path wakes the listener immediately; a 30 s fallback poll covers missed notifications across reconnects. `vt=300s` redelivers the message to the next consumer if the current one disconnects before deleting — that is the survives-eviction guarantee. Replaces the prior HTTP long-poll (`top.com.runner-from-backend-inbox`, deleted).

Per-tool-call hook: BeforeToolCall blocks until 200 or the 2 s deadline; AfterToolCall and ArtifactRegistered are queued and fired-and-forget. Body signed with HMAC-SHA256 over `f"{ts_ms}.".encode() + body` using the per-runner `runner_secret`.

Streamable-HTTP MCP (2025-03-26 spec). The agent's `Tool`s are dynamically discovered via `list_tools_sync()` against this endpoint; each tool call from the LLM round-trips here. Contract is owned by the external party; not documented in interfaces.xml.

Strands model adapter (`AnthropicModel` / `GeminiModel`) streams completion tokens back to the runner, which translates them into AG-UI `TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT` deltas. Provider contract is owned by Anthropic / Google; not documented in interfaces.xml.

environment.name: dev
environment.note: Local docker-compose stack on the operator's machine. All units present. Bridge network `kloc` (explicit name). Backend on host port 8002, frontend on 3000, MinIO API on 9010 + console 9011, Postgres on 5432. `top.kloc-intelligence-mcp` is reached via `host.docker.internal:8765`; the operator brings its compose stack up separately.

environment.note: End-to-end smoke profile (`docker-compose.smoke.yml`). Same shape as dev; used by CI for happy-path checks.
